Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. We will provide instructions at that time for queuing up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Reyes, Chief Medical Officer; Lisa Thompson, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year, trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, labor costs as a percentage of revenue, impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, and revenue per admission trends and drivers.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach to growth and efficiency in a dynamic healthcare environment. To dive deeper into the financial underpinnings of these achievements, I'll now turn the call over to Steve Harlan.

Steve Harlan:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. As Emily highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter across the board. Let me start by providing detailed color on those seven key aspects before walking through our overall financial results.

First, on the status of our ongoing and planned acquisitions and divestitures, M&A continues to be a cornerstone of our inorganic growth strategy in this fragmented healthcare services and hospitals sector. We're zeroed in on bolt-on opportunities that strengthen our continuum of care, unlock operational synergies, and position us for the shift to value-based care and outpatient dominance.

On the acquisition front, we're excited about two deals in advanced stages that align perfectly with our pillars of geographic densification, ambulatory expansion, and behavioral health growth. The pending acquisition of Southeast Regional Hospitals, a five-hospital system with 850 licensed beds mainly in the Carolinas and Georgia, remains on track. We signed a definitive agreement in late first quarter for $1.2 billion, pending regulatory approvals. Due diligence has validated our projections: it adds $450 million in annualized revenue with a 4.2% EBITDA margin before synergies. We now expect $65 million in annual synergies by year two, from 15% procurement savings via our Vizient GPO leverage, centralized revenue cycle management through Epic integration, and shared supply chain analytics using AI tools from our prior Cerner playbook.

Regulatory progress is solid—FTC and state AG filings are done, with early Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance. We look for a Q4 close, delivering 5% accretion to adjusted EPS in fiscal 2025. This expands our Southeast presence to 28% of total beds, capitalizing on 52% Medicare Advantage penetration in the Carolinas per CMS stats. SRH's ortho and cardiology strengths will integrate with our outpatient joint ventures, building on 18% year-over-year case growth in our 12 existing ASCs this quarter.

We're also moving forward with the tuck-in acquisition of Coastal Behavioral Health Network, eight freestanding psych facilities and 15 outpatient clinics in Florida and Alabama, at $425 million. Heads of terms signed in May, with a binding LOI imminent. It brings $180 million in revenue at 12% EBITDA margins, strong amid sector compression to 8-10% from labor issues. We forecast $25 million in day-one synergies via nurse staffing optimization with our predictive scheduling algorithm—that cut overtime 22% system-wide last year—and cross-referrals from our 42 acute care hospitals.

Demand surges 30% for inpatient psych beds post-COVID per SAMHSA, with supply lagging at 11 beds per 100,000 in the Southeast. Target close is Q1 2025 after Florida AHCA review, boosting our behavioral health revenue share from 7% to 11%, diversifying from inpatient where CMI pressures from downcoding linger.

On divestitures, we stay disciplined for portfolio optimization. In Q3, we completed the sale of three underperforming rural Midwest hospitals—320 beds—to a local non-profit for $180 million cash. They generated $120 million revenue with negative 2% margins, hit by 15% uncompensated care and outdated facilities. This yielded a $50 million book gain, lifted ROIC 150 basis points, and frees capital for better returns.

Proceeds split 60% to debt paydown—aiming for 3.2x leverage by year-end from 3.6x—and 40% to share repurchases under our $500 million program. This echoes industry moves, with Kaufman Hall noting 25% more rural divestitures as for-profits shift to urban/suburban amid weak rural funds.

Our pipeline is robust with $3-4 billion dry powder, including $1.5 billion revolver capacity. Priorities: ambulatory and physician roll-ups targeting $800 million across 10-15 deals, like JV expansions with Tenet-style Conifer for 20 ASCs in Dallas-Fort Worth and Phoenix—outpatient volumes up 12-15% per MGMA. LOIs out on three, $250 million closes eyed for 2025 at 20% IRR via site-of-service savings as payers push 50% to lower-cost sites.

Tech tuck-ins get $500 million, like a $150 million Change Healthcare analytics carve-out to boost denial management to 92% auto-approval with NLP. Regional builds target Midwest hospital pairs at $600-700 million in CON-friendly Ohio/Indiana, adding 1,200 beds and 15% synergies via our CareBridge ACO, which saved $120 million last year.

We're East Coast-focused at 65% EBITDA but eyeing West Coast via UHS divestitures amid Medi-Cal shifts. Deal velocity up 35% QoQ per PitchBook despite rates, with $150 billion PE dry powder, though antitrust lingers post-HCA cases. These de-risk via MA leverage (42% now, 50% by 2026), cooling wage growth to 4.5%, and Epic MyChart at 85%. Risks: integration, FY2025 IPPS 2.9% lump but -0.3% cut. Overall, accretive M&A supports 6-8% EPS growth in 2025 sans deals.

Next, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for Q4 and FY 2025. Same-facility strips M&A, focusing organic across our 180-hospital and 1,200+ ambulatory sites. For Q4, inpatient admissions guide 2.0-3.0%, on 2.7% Q3 strength from ortho/cardio up 5-7% via Medtronic/Intuitive Surgical robotics. CMI up 1.5-2.0% QoQ on complex TAVR/CABG, 65+ cohort now 42% of admissions.

Outpatient visits 4.5-5.5%, via ASCs and OneDay platform for same-day discharges. YTD outpatient +6.2%, doubling inpatient pace like HCA/Tenet. Revenue growth 4.0-5.0%, RPA flat to +1.0%, assuming steady IPPS, 2-3% commercial uplift. Mix stable: 45% gov, 50% commercial, 5% other. Monitoring GLP-1 bariatric softness.

Sunbelt leads: Texas/Florida 6-7% on telehealth up 25% YoY; Southeast 5% via UHC VBC. Midwest/Northeast 1-2% headwinds from flu/ASC competition, offset by ortho robotics regaining share. FY2025 revenue 5.0-6.0%, volumes 3.0-4.0% (inpt 2.5-3.5%, outpt 5-6%), plus CMI/pricing. Assumes 3.4% OPPS, $250M capex for AI RCM yielding AR improvements. Volume Velocity invests $500M in pods like neuro suites/Stryker, oncology CAR-T. Site-neutral tailwinds shift 15% revenue to ASCs. Risks: RN turnover 18%, Medicaid redeterms. Outpaces 3.5% sector consensus.

Moving to trends in payer mix shifts and their revenue impact. Payer mix drives revenue quality amid VBC and MA growth. Q3 inpatient equivalent: Medicare 38% net patient revenue, up 200 bps YoY; Medicaid 14% steady; commercial/managed 40% down from 42%; self-pay/other 8%. Consistent across 45 hospitals.

MA at 52% of Medicare lives matches CMS 33M+ enrollment. MA rates down 2-3% YoY on stars/blending. Florida/Texas MA volume up 3 pts QoQ on snowbirds/recovery; Midwest commercial stickier at 45%. Retained 85% Medicaid at-risk via engagement platform despite redeterms.

Commercial headwinds from No Surprises/site-neutral upped OON denials 15% per Change. Yet revenue +7.2% YoY to $2.8B, mix added $45M or 1.6%. RPA $13,950 vs $14,200 absent shift, offset by 4% CMI to 1.85, 5% outpt volume, 2.5% commercial rates.

Blended yield up 50 bps to 42.5%, denials to 4.2%. MA HCC recapture +$1,200/1,000 MM via 3M/Epic. VBC at 25% commercial via ACO REACH yielded $28M savings. Bundles with Humana for joints target 10% CMI. AI RCM with Waystar/Cerner cut A/R to 38 days.

Expect Medicare 39-40% YE, margins 12.5%. VBC/shared savings, counseling app converting 22% uninsured.

On net patient revenue YoY and QoQ: $2.82B, +8.2% YoY, +2.1% QoQ. Beats amid IPPS cut/MA denials like HCA/Tenet. YoY +$215M from Q3'23 $2.605B: admissions 142,500 +4.7%, days 1.125M +5.9% on 12% outpt shift. RPA $25,060 +3.4%, CMI 1.92 +1.8 pts on cardiac/ortho/neuro.

Commercial 52% +5.2%; Medicare 38% slip on acuity/MA auths -15-20%; Medicaid 8% offset by supplements in TX/FL 18 sites. Sunbelt +6.9% on 7.2% admits, FL Blue JV; Midwest/Northeast +3.1% on flu/labor.

QoQ on seasonality/RCM: collections 97.8%, Epic AI/3M denials -22% to 4.1%, Olive prior auth A/R to 42 days. High-acuity playbook: oncology/transplant >15% margins, ASCs to 65. Guide Q4 7-9% YoY, upside from Carolinas acq.

Labor costs as % revenue: 54.8%, +210 bps YoY from 52.7%, down from Q1 55.6%; adj 54.2% ex bonuses. Total $1.42B, RN wages +7.2% on 100K vacancies per AHA. Agency 12% of labor $170M, like HCA 11-13%, Tenet 15%.

Hourly $48.75 core +28% benefits $62.40; HPPD 8.9 from 9.4 on acuity CMI 1.82. Southeast 53.1% competition/expansion; Midwest 52.4% low unions; CA 58.2% staffing mandates.

Burnout turnover 25% RNs, CBAs 5.5%, IPPS 2.9% lags 4.1% RPA. Initiatives: LeanTaaS AI scheduling -15% ineff, -0.3 HPPD; tele/virtual nursing -10-15% RN hours, $25M save. Care program $50M bonuses/tuition down turnover 18% QoQ. Agency caps with AMN/Cross Country.

Q3 guide 54.5-55.0%, FY 54.0-54.5%. Risks flu/staffing scrutiny. Tech/talent for margins like CHS.

Impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement: VBC 28% net revenue $1.2B TTM, up from 18%, double industry 12% vs HCA/Tenet. MSSP Track 3 ACOs 15 hospitals $45M savings +25% YoY, 12% readmits vs 15.5% national, 7.2% uplift FFS.

BPCI-A joints/cardiac $32M gains, episodes $28K vs $34.2K benchmark, 65% preferred post-acute -1.2 LOS. Commercial Optum/Anthem 150K lives $210M +5.5%, $18M incentives +40%, $12M downside.

Northeast 42% VBC +9%; rural SE 15%, countered tele $50M/Aledade. Epic/Google AI 82% readmit predict, MIPS +22% $15M. VBC 11% EBITDA vs FFS 4-6%.

Tiered: 60% upside, 30% two-sided stop-loss, 10% cap. YE2025 35% +$250M EBITDA. Challenges drugs/labor, offset SNFs/CIN/M&A. 8-10% uplifts aligning outcomes.

Finally, revenue per admission trends/drivers: Consolidated RPA $15,420 Q3, +6.8% YoY, +2.1% QoQ on 142K admits flat YoY, revenue $2.19B +7.2%. Quality focus.

CMI +4.1% to 1.92 on comorbidities DRGs, ortho/neuro +12%, CDI/3M AI +$42M 92% capture. Commercial 48% + from 44%, 7-9% hikes; Medicare 32% $12,800 +5.4%; Medicaid 18% +supps; denials 4.2%.

ALOS -3.5% to 4.6, obs +15%; surgical +11% cath $22K; imaging/pharm +9% proton/biosimilars; Vizient implants +2.8% vs 5.1%. SE $16,200 +8.9% aging/ortho; TX $15,900; Midwest $14,300 +3.2%; West tele neuro.

Acuity Engine $250M Tempus/Waystar +0.07 CMI, bundles 10% uplift. FY24 $15,450-15,650 5.5-7%; risks IPPS/MedPAC. Outperforms peers.

With that foundation, net revenue for Q3 was $2.82 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year. Growth stemmed from higher volumes, payer dynamics, and revenue cycle gains. Operating expenses totaled $2.45 billion, or 86.9% of net revenue. We're managing costs tightly while investing in growth, especially labor optimization.

Net income was $225 million, or $2.15 per diluted share. We're pleased and confident in hitting yearly goals.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reyes for clinical updates.

Dr. Michael Reyes:
Thank you, Steve. Good morning. We're advancing clinical outcomes and satisfaction markedly. Our Comprehensive Care Coordination program delivered an 18% reduction in readmission rates, surpassing benchmarks. We're harnessing technology for better experiences and coordination, expanding telehealth platforms with 30% utilization growth and remote patient monitoring for high-risk chronic patients, integrating AI for predictive alerts.

Following that, Lisa will update on operations.

Lisa Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Reyes. We're streamlining across our network. Key initiatives include AI-powered workforce scheduling and centralized supply chain consolidation, yielding $40 million in savings and 15% better patient throughput, with ER wait times down 20% and bed turnover optimized.

Next, David on strategy.

David Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Our priorities center on network growth, partnerships, and tech innovation. Beyond M&A, we're forming JVs with payers for bundled ortho and pursuing digital health alliances to enhance service lines in high-growth MSAs.

After that, Raj on IT and cybersecurity.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, David. Our IT infrastructure is secure and scalable, safeguarding patient data. Recent enhancements include zero-trust architecture, AI-driven threat detection, and advanced compliance tools, ensuring HIPAA adherence with no incidents this year.

Now, back to Emily.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you, team. At this time, we'll open for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of recent cybersecurity threats on operations and patient data?

Raj Singh:
Good morning, John. We've seen no material impact from recent threats. Our proactive measures, including $50 million invested in AI monitoring and multi-factor encryption across systems, prevented any breaches. Patient data remains fully secure, and we're exceeding compliance standards.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson:
Thanks. What are your plans for expanding telehealth and remote patient monitoring?

Dr. Michael Reyes:
Good morning, Mary. We're planning to double telehealth capacity next year through platform upgrades and provider hires, integrating AI diagnostics for faster triage. RPM will expand to 50,000 patients, partnering with wearables for real-time CHF management, targeting 25% cost savings in readmits.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
Appreciate it. More details on strategic partnerships and business impact?

David Patel:
Hi Mike. Key partnerships include a new oncology JV with Novartis for CAR-T delivery and expanded VBC with Humana covering 200,000 lives. These should add $150 million revenue by 2026, diversifying high-margin services and boosting MA leverage.

Operator:
Our next question from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Any update on labor cost outlook given agency pressures?

Steve Harlan:
Hi Lisa. As detailed, we're guiding FY labor at 54.0-54.5% with agency below 10% by Q4 via internal ramps and contracts. Tech like LeanTaaS is key, positioning for expansion.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
